releases.name: v1.3.13
tweets: OpenCode v1.3.13 released. TL;DR: mostly a correctness release; hardens async instance context across Effect runtimes; makes session revert/summary Effect-native; fixes project-scoped paths for worktrees, formatting, config writes, and event routing.

Under the hood, the active project/worktree context is now attached to managed runtimes, so Effect fibers can recover instance state even after deferred resumes outside AsyncLocalStorage. Finalizer cleanup also restores context before touching prompt state.

That mainly affects session lifecycle code: revert and diff summarization now run through shared services, assistant/compaction messages record the right cwd/root, and rollback cleanup can reliably trim later turns or later parts from the chosen point.

Lower-level tooling got the same treatment: DB transaction side effects stay bound to the instance; formatter subprocesses, config writes, and worktree creation use the right repo/dir; global event streams now report the correct directory too.

releases.name: v1.3.14
tweets: OpenCode v1.3.14 released. TL;DR: git-backed review modes are back; provider/model wiring is smarter; TUI/plugin + desktop surfaces are more extensible; runtime got sturdier around snapshots, revert, and process control.

Review got real git awareness again. Core now exposes working-tree and merge-base diff modes, and the app restores both git and branch review modes. Review rendering also lazy-mounts nearby diffs, and line comments can @mention repo paths.

Provider/model plumbing changed in useful ways: GitHub Copilot OAuth now refreshes models from Copilot's /models endpoint, pulling real limits and capabilities while preserving local metadata. Plugins can also replace a provider's model catalog.

Integration got tighter. Non-OpenCode model calls now carry x-session-affinity and x-parent-session-id. ACP streams add message IDs to chunks and emit user_message_chunk too, so external clients can correlate both sides of a turn without heuristics.

TUI plugins got a bigger surface: they can replace or extend the home/session prompt, get prompt refs for focus/set/submit, and inject right-side prompt UI. Theme-only packages now load via oc-themes even without a TUI entrypoint.

Runtime hardening: snapshot diffing batches git blob reads; revert restores the prior snapshot before re-reverting; OpenAI-compatible tool-call loops no longer stop early on bad finish reasons; the JS SDK now tears down Windows child trees cleanly.

Desktop/ops cleanup: Electron now loads login-shell env before launching the sidecar, adds a real context menu plus fuller macOS Go/View menus, reads macOS MDM managed prefs as config, and can auto-write heap snapshots past 2GB RSS.
Compare: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/compare/v1.3.13...v1.3.14

releases.name: v1.3.15
tweets: OpenCode v1.3.15 released. TL;DR: fixes npm installs in compiled builds; the win carries into npm-backed providers/plugins/LSP/formatters; trims Kimi prompt redundancy; otherwise this is a small patch release.

The main behavioral change is in OpenCode's npm layer. It now skips lifecycle scripts during reify/install, and the compiled build no longer bakes in a node-gyp resolution path. Result: fewer install failures from the shipped binary.

Why it matters: this same npm path is reused for npm-backed model providers, npm plugins, auto-downloaded language servers, formatter binaries, and plugin project setup. One runtime fix improves several extension and tooling flows.
There is also a small Kimi-specific cleanup: its system prompt drops a duplicated skills section. No new capability here, but less redundant prompt overhead for Kimi sessions.

releases.name: v1.3.16
tweets: OpenCode v1.3.16 released. TL;DR: ACP session controls are more protocol-native. Console-managed providers and org switching now show up in the TUI. Plugin resolution is sturdier on npm alias/git specs and Windows. Token/provider accounting bugs were fixed.

ACP got more protocol-native session control: session responses now publish selectable model/mode options, and OpenCode implements ACP's config-option setter to change them. ACP clients need less OpenCode-specific logic.

There is also a new experimental Console API surface: fetch active Console-managed provider metadata, list available orgs across accounts, and switch the active org. The generated JS SDK/OpenAPI was updated with those endpoints.

TUI/provider UX now consumes that state end to end. Console-managed providers are labeled with the active org, blocked from local reconnect flows, and a new org switcher shows up when multiple orgs exist.

TUI input behavior is more controllable too: mouse capture can be disabled via tui.json or OPENCODE_DISABLE_MOUSE, and on Windows Ctrl+Z now defaults to prompt undo while terminal suspend is suppressed when unsupported.

Plugin/package resolution is more robust. OpenCode now parses plugin specs with npm-package-arg, so aliases and git/npm protocol specs resolve correctly, and Windows cache paths sanitize illegal characters that used to break installs.

Model/runtime fixes: Azure options are sent under both openai and azure namespaces so settings survive either AI SDK path, and usage accounting no longer double-counts reasoning tokens. Vertex Anthropic cache-write tokens are now separated too.

releases.name: v1.3.17
tweets: OpenCode v1.3.17 released. TL;DR: Cloudflare auth/setup is much clearer. Windows TUI input backs out a kitty-keyboard workaround. Zen normalizes IPv6 and simplifies anonymous rate limiting.

Provider/auth: cloudflare-workers-ai and cloudflare-ai-gateway now prompt for missing Cloudflare account and gateway IDs during auth, not just a token. Those fields are stored with API auth and exposed through the auth API and JS SDK.

Cloudflare provider setup is less opaque: IDs can come from saved auth metadata or env, baseURL overrides bypass the ID check, and missing IDs now raise explicit setup errors instead of silently refusing to load.

TUI: the Windows-specific kitty keyboard workaround was reverted. OpenCode removes the special Ctrl+V key-release path and drops the win32-only kitty event config, simplifying terminal input handling.

Zen backend: x-real-ip is normalized before rate limiting, collapsing IPv6 addresses to a stable prefix. Anonymous free-tier limiting no longer branches on a special header and now uses default or per-model daily limits directly.

releases.name: v1.4.0
tweets: OpenCode v1.4.0 released. TL;DR: remote workspace transport got a real proxy layer; subagent UX is much better; review diffs moved to patch-based rendering; OTLP observability landed.

Core transport changed a lot. Workspaces now resolve to local or remote targets, and remote ones proxy both HTTP and WebSocket traffic instead of relying on custom fetch-only adaptors. The control plane is less Bun-specific now.

OTLP export is now first-class: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT plus optional headers attaches a runtime-wide observability layer with service and environment metadata. The runtime also abstracts PTY handling across Bun and Node backends.

Tooling/runtime got cleaned up. The old batch tool is gone, task and skill descriptions are generated against the active agent's permissions, and TUI plugins no longer manage workspace-scoped clients. Workspace routing is centralized in core now.

Subagents got real product work. Child sessions now show parent/task context in the header, disable inappropriate composer and follow-up flows, and the TUI worker can keep multiple event streams alive instead of swapping a single global stream.

Review data is now patch-first. Session snapshots and live VCS diffs use separate patch-based schemas, the review UI normalizes both paths, lazily mounts visible diffs, and adds a render-anyway guard for very large changes.

Prompt attachments now treat PDFs as first-class media: file pickers accept them, drag/drop and optimistic request assembly preserve them, and prompt restoration rebuilds PDF attachments from stored message parts.

Fixes worth noting: plain-text rate-limit failures now retry correctly, including Alibaba-style messages; model variants stay scoped to the selected model; login errors are more actionable; and opencode run gained --dangerously-skip-permissions.

• Compaction now seamlessly anchors off previous summaries, intelligently hiding prior compaction turns from the prompt to maximize token budgets.
• Turn splitting is now calculated at the message boundary, preventing token overflow when a single large turn exceeds the preservation budget.
• Truncates tool output at 2000 characters during summarization passes to prevent context window explosion.

Models & Tools
• Added reasoning variant support (`reasoningEffort`) for Mistral Small (`mistral-small-latest`, `mistral-small-2603`).
• Text tools (`edit`, `write`, `apply_patch`) now strictly preserve Byte Order Marks (BOM) during file read/write round-trips.
• The TUI now fails fast with clear errors when attaching to a corrupted or invalid session, preventing hangs.
• Fixed project caching for bare Git repositories by correctly resolving the Git common directory.
